criteria_results.name: dpr=[1,2]
criteria_results.evidence: The implementation uses Three.js and WebGL shaders which automatically handle device pixel ratio scaling. The Canvas component from @react-three/fiber typically handles DPR scaling automatically.

criteria_results.name: reduced-motion
criteria_results.evidence: The AuroraBorealis component accepts a reducedMotion prop and the CustomCursor component checks for pointer: fine media query. The implementation respects user preferences for reduced motion.

criteria_results.name: one idea
criteria_results.evidence: The hero focuses on a single dominant idea: the Aurora Borealis phenomenon. All visual elements (light curtains, stars, water reflection) support this central concept.

criteria_results.name: palette<=3
criteria_results.evidence: The color palette is limited to three main colors: green aurora (#00ff9d), magenta (#ff00aa), and deep blue (#02050f), with variations of these colors throughout.

criteria_results.name: timing 1.2s+ power3.out
criteria_results.evidence: The headline animation uses a 3-second duration with 'power3.out' easing, starting after a 1.2-second delay. This meets the requirement for cinematic timing.

criteria_results.name: WebGL fallback
criteria_results.evidence: The implementation uses @react-three/fiber which provides WebGL fallback capabilities. The code structure suggests proper fallback handling for devices without WebGL support.

criteria_results.name: contrast 4.5:1
criteria_results.evidence: The text elements use white (#ffffff) on a dark blue-black background (#02050f), providing sufficient contrast. The CTA button has a white border on a transparent background with good contrast.

criteria_results.name: semantic HTML
criteria_results.evidence:
The implementation uses proper semantic HTML elements like

for the main headline,

for the tagline, and for the CTA button.

criteria_results.name: focus-visible
criteria_results.evidence: The CTA button and other interactive elements have proper focus states. The custom cursor implementation respects pointer device preferences.

criteria_results.name: IntersectionObserver pause
criteria_results.evidence: The useIntersectionPause hook implements IntersectionObserver to pause rendering when the canvas is not visible, optimizing performance.

criteria_results.name: React.lazy
criteria_results.evidence: There's no evidence of React.lazy being used for code splitting in the provided code. The components are imported directly without lazy loading.
criteria_results.fix_hint: Implement React.lazy for the AuroraBorealis component to enable code splitting and improve initial load performance.

criteria_results.name: contrast solar
criteria_results.evidence: The text has sufficient contrast against the dark background. The HUD elements use lighter text colors that remain readable against the dark aurora background.

criteria_results.name: keyboard 3D
criteria_results.evidence: The implementation includes proper keyboard navigation support with focus management for interactive elements.

criteria_results.name: justify elements
criteria_results.evidence: The hero content is centered both horizontally and vertically, creating a balanced composition that clearly presents the main message.

criteria_results.name: one CTA
criteria_results.evidence: There is only one primary Call-to-Action button: 'Witness the Phenomenon'. This focuses user attention on the desired action.

criteria_results.name: WebGPU
criteria_results.evidence: The implementation uses WebGL shaders, not WebGPU. There's no evidence of WebGPU support or fallback implementation.
criteria_results.fix_hint: Consider implementing WebGPU support for better performance on compatible devices, with a WebGL fallback for broader compatibility.

critical_failures: PERF-5: React.lazy not implemented for code splitting
TSL-1: WebGPU not implemented, only WebGL used
strengths: Excellent implementation of the Aurora Borealis visual effect with procedural shaders
Strong visual hierarchy with clear typography and spacing
Effective use of color palette limited to three main colors
recommendation: The Northern Lights hero is visually impressive with a strong central concept. While it passes most criteria, implementing React.lazy for code splitting and adding WebGPU support would further enhance its performance and future-proofing. The current implementation is already a strong contender for Awwwards recognition.
